items.note: Page dated 7 Feb 2019 states no free parking spaces any more inside the Alleenring and in Bornheim, Bockenheim, Dornbusch, Gallus; downtown EUR 1 per 20 min, outer EUR 0.50 per 20 min; resident permit EUR 50 for 2 years. Fetched page title appears as 'Keine kostenlosen Parkplätze mehr in Frankfurt - Neues Parkraumkonzept wird eingeführt' (order reversed vs draft); URL slug matches draft order, so left unchanged.

Page dated 28 Jan 2022: parliament approved stepwise closure Alte Brücke to Untermainbrücke over four years; weekend/overnight closures first, full closure in Hessian school holidays; full closure conditional on a diversion concept protecting other districts, esp. Sachsenhausen. Headline is 'Mainkai-Sperrung kommt zurück' with 'Stadtverordnetenversammlung' as the URL-slug prefix; acceptable.
Page dated 1 Sep 2023: ten weeks closure, reopened 1 Sep 2023, disruption mainly from big events like Mainfest/Mainuferfest, detailed traffic evaluation expected in October. All matched.

Page (9 Jan 2024) supports EUR 50 to EUR 240 for two years from 10 Jan 2024, first increase in 20 years, parliament decision 20 July 2023. The 'October 2025 report ... no plans for further increases' is NOT on this page (no mention of Oct 2025 or future increases); it comes from a different (hessenschau) source. source_title is a mix of two pages.
items.corrected_text: On 10 January 2024 the price of a Frankfurt resident parking permit rose from EUR 50 to EUR 240 for two years, the first adjustment in 20 years, following a city parliament decision of 20 July 2023.
items.corrected_title: Ab Mittwoch: Anwohnerparken in Frankfurt wird fast fünfmal so teuer

items.note: Page dated 8 May 2025: two-thirds majority, executive approved March 2025, 80% of trips sustainable by 2035 up from 67%, eleven key measures including raising parking fees. No amounts are given on the page.
Page dated 26 Sep 2025: about 3,000 new P+R spaces; Hessen-Center Enkheim 500+, Römerhof ~640, Praunheim 600+, Gateway Gardens possibly ~1,000; schedule still open, no dates given.

Page dated 11 May 2022: city, ABG (parent of PBG) and Mainova; 284 new charge points (wallboxes max 22 kW) in 11 public garages; existing 16 grow to about 300; build-out planned to start and finish in 2023; use always subject to parking fees. 'AC' is implied by wallbox, not stated in the fetched text.

Article (18 Dec 2023) is in future tense: the first 150+ points were to go into operation 'this month', not that they had. Page lists Konstabler 40, Konrad-Adenauer-Straße 31, Goetheplatz 30; second stage of 130 points planned for first half 2024 (Schiller Passage 19, Am Gericht 34, Börse 30, DomRömer 28 seen). The counts 'six garages' and 'five garages' could not be confirmed from the page.
items.corrected_text: In December 2023 the city said the first 150-plus of its new AC charge points in public garages, including 40 at Parkhaus Konstabler, 31 at Konrad-Adenauer-Straße and 30 at Tiefgarage Goetheplatz, were due to go into operation that month. A second stage of a further 130 points, including garages such as Schiller Passage, Am Gericht, Börse and DomRömer, was planned for completion in the first half of 2024.

items.note: Page dated 23 Feb 2026: tender for about 400 AC and 20 DC points; 2,133 public points (1,890 AC, 243 DC) per Bundesnetzagentur data cited by city; AC points up more than 350% Jan 2023 to Jan 2026. The word 'regular' in the draft is not on the page but is harmless; 'next phase' is what the page says.

Vendor page dated 14 Nov 2023: plate recognition and customer portal for registered long-term parkers, project covers 12 garages with over 6,700 spaces; PBG about 7 million short-term and 10,000 long-term parkers a year (PBG total 18,000 spaces).

IHK press release 13 Sep 2024: system deactivated; disconnected from city IT in 2022 over security gaps; data entered by hand for over two years; city says construction of new system can start mid-2026 at the earliest.

Page dated 30 Dec 2025: over 3,200 businesses, 936 retail, about 43% of visitors from outside Frankfurt mostly by car, weak consumer demand and online competition named as pressures. Actual page title is longer than the draft's.
items.corrected_title: Neuerscheinung Zahlenspiegel Frankfurter Innenstadt 2025: Handel bleibt Motor der City – Transformation konsequent weiterdenken

items.note: Page dated 9 Mar 2026: 11,023,600 overnight stays, -1% vs 2024 (stays; guests -0.4%), 2024 boosted by men's Euro, domestic record 4.2 million, international -6.7%.

Page dated 21 Jan 2026: RMV carried 839 million, more than ever; 650,000 used Deutschlandtickets; the 8.3% growth refers to Deutschlandticket subscribers in 2025 (draft wording is compatible but attaches it loosely). Fetched title 'RMV erreicht Fahrgast-Rekord'; draft's 'Verkehr in Frankfurt:' prefix is likely the section/slug, left unchanged.

corrected_summary: Frankfurt's 2025 Masterplan Mobilität lists higher parking fees among its key measures, and the city has a park-and-ride concept with about 3,000 planned new spaces. Resident-permit fees rose from EUR 50 to EUR 240 for two years in January 2024. The city and ABG announced plans for hundreds of new charging points in public garages from 2023, PBG has introduced plate-recognition entry in 12 garages, and the IHK reported in 2024 that the municipal parking guidance system was switched off, with the city saying a replacement could start construction mid-2026 at the earliest.
